correctness.rationale: The centered monomial has variance α²/((2α+1)(α+1)²)>0, giving the stated real symmetric kernel, including for complex data. The L∞ upper bound is sharp by applying to the sign of a maximizing kernel row and using continuity even if that row is at an endpoint; duality then gives the L1 norm. In x^α the row mass is convex; the value at the monomial mean is 1, below both endpoint values, so the segments split at that point exclude every interior maximizer. Each endpoint kernel has a single zero. At the left endpoint its positive integral is (α+1)h₀/α; at the right endpoint its negative mass is h₁. The norm formulas follow using total mass 1. The right branch increases by log(1+s)>s/(1+s); the left branch decreases because in t=1/α the derivative of its logarithmic positive mass is 2z+log(1−z)>0 for z=1/(t+2) in (0,1/2). Their equality at α=1 gives the exact switch and unique minimum 5/3. The diagonal is strictly convex in x^α, with endpoint heights (1+1/α)² and 2(α+1), and these have the same switch. Simplifying the logarithms as α tends to zero or infinity verifies the claimed asymptotics. Independent inverse-Gram quadrature and diagonal evaluations reproduced the endpoint values at eight exponents.
residual_risks: The numerical comparison is a cross-check; the analytic proof covers every α>0. The claim is about the fixed Lebesgue L²-orthogonal projector with a constant basis function, not the least norm of arbitrary projections.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Take the two simplex coordinates (x,1−x) with parameters (η,1), η=1/α. If η>1 the smaller parameter is at x=0; if η<1 it is at x=1. The integral defining F_A has exactly the submitted endpoint values when specialized to this beta law (there is one sign change and a power antiderivative). The diagonal is convex and evaluation at the vertices gives A(A+1)/α_i−A, yielding both submitted peak branches by substitution.

originality.rationale: The central sharp endpoint norm and maximizer classification have demonstrable coverage by the distinct indexed affine Dirichlet theorem 5c9fbf13aa23. There is an isometric change of variable, a direct specialization of its exact theorem, and a mechanical evaluation of its diagonal kernel. This is a same-calendar-day catalogue record; coverage is definite, but earlier priority and ordering are not established, and neither is claimed here. Its balanced minimization at fixed concentration does not itself show the variable-concentration optimum in this record.
